openings.claim: A reconciliation ledger with a missing-evidence matrix can preserve all rows and produce twelve documented decisions while directing at most three follow-up requests.
openings.delta: Extend the incumbent row ledger with dependencies between unresolved batch decisions and specific missing fields or records. Use supplied conversion, status definitions, cutoffs and explicit supersession links before deciding quantities. Keep duplicate, unmatched and superseded rows visible. Group requests only when the same missing field or record genuinely blocks several decisions. The nearest rival converts quantities and prefers the newer report.
openings.prediction: The awkward replacement should remain disputed unless supplied evidence establishes its correspondence across row identifiers; matching quantities alone cannot establish identity. Removing a supersession reference or introducing an undefined status should add an explicit dependency, potentially reducing definite resolutions. Relative to newer-report preference, expect fewer unsupported definite claims; grouped dependencies may reduce request counts without concealing unresolved batches. These effects are unmeasured.
openings.probe: Within sixty total reviewer minutes, share ingestion across the ledger and rival, derive and freeze outputs for both supplied copies, then spend the extra twenty minutes comparing against the sealed key. Count resolved batches, unsupported definite claims and requests; inspect evidence citations and preservation of every row. Defeat conditions are unsupported definite claims, missing batch decisions, dropped rows, more than three requests, or inability to finish the full review within sixty minutes. If both variants cannot be completed within the stipulated resources, comparative feasibility remains unestablished; merely stopping is not an informative test.
assumptions: Actual records and workload are not provided here; combined variant execution may exceed available review capacity.
Requests name missing fields or records and affected batches. Unrequested gaps remain explicit.
A bounded disagreement lists supported candidate quantities and any unknown extent; never infer missing quantities from neighboring batches.

assessment: This is a workflow proposal and probe, not deployment or measured success. Missing linkage and undefined status may prevent definite reconciliation; twelve explicit decisions remain required.

lineage.reason: Preserve evidence-led reconciliation; add shared missing-evidence requests and make combined probe capacity explicit.
